about: The production source of the film: who and where everything is, how it looks and sounds, every shot with its length, framing, action, words and sound, and every number the film speaks. tools/film.py compiles it, with the screenplay, into the shot list, the prompt pack for text-to-video and image-to-video tools, the reference-sheet prompts, the cards and overlays, the industry PDF and the Final Draft file, and checks it against the screenplay and the records.

tools._note: The clip lengths each tool published when this file was written (November 2026). Tools change: read the tool's own page before generating. A shot longer than a tool's longest clip is generated in parts or extended from its last frame; a shot is generated at the shortest allowed length at or above its own and trimmed in the edit.

style.base: Photoreal live-action cinema, shot on 35mm film with fine grain, natural motivated light, shallow depth of field, restrained color grade, steady composed camera

palettes.night_storm: night in a tropical storm: deep blue-black, sodium-amber streetlight, rain streaks catching the light
palettes.bedroom_night: 3 a.m. darkness lit only by cool blue phone and laptop glow, a slow ceiling-fan shadow
palettes.day_storm: overcast pre-storm daylight, flat grey-green, wind moving everything
palettes.office_storm: pewter storm light through glass walls, cool and flat, warm interior practical lamps
palettes.ed_dusk: cyan-white hospital fluorescent light, dusk blue outside the ambulance bay
palettes.data_hall: cool blue-white LED light, black racks, thousands of tiny green and blue indicator lights
palettes.generator: after the power cut: dim amber emergency light mixed with blue monitor glow
palettes.ct_room: cool clinical light, the white ring of the scanner, monitor glow
palettes.dawn: pink-gold dawn after a storm, wet surfaces reflecting, clean air
palettes.car_dawn: pink-gold dawn through a windshield, laptop glow on a tired face
palettes.morning_garage: soft warm morning light through an open garage door, dust in the air

style.signs: status lights are shapes: a green circle means working, a yellow diamond means heading for its line, a red octagon means over its line
negative: legible words on any screen, paper or sign

del.name: DEL
del.look: Haitian-American woman, 34, deep brown skin, close-cropped natural black hair, tired dark eyes with shadows under them, slim build, small gold stud earrings
del.wear: charcoal crew-neck sweatshirt, black jeans, a navy hospital lanyard with an ID badge
del.voice: low, dry, quick; Florida in the vowels; goes quiet when it matters

ray.name: RAY
ray.look: Haitian-born man, 69, dark brown skin, close-cut grey hair, short white stubble, broad forearms, reading glasses on a black cord
ray.wear: faded blue work shirt with rolled sleeves, khaki work trousers, worn leather work boots
ray.voice: warm, unhurried, a Haitian Kreyòl cadence; teaches by showing

theo.name: THEO
theo.look: man, 46, light skin, close-cropped sandy hair greying at the temples, clean-shaven, upright military bearing
theo.wear: plain navy zip fleece over a white collared shirt

sloane.name: SLOANE
sloane.look: woman, 38, light olive skin, sleek dark bob, precise makeup, poised
sloane.wear: tailored ivory blazer over a black top, thin gold watch, a tablet in hand
sloane.voice: warm, polished, never rushed; believes her deck

nadia.name: NADIA
nadia.look: Puerto Rican woman, 52, light-brown skin, shoulder-length curly dark hair streaked with grey, reading glasses pushed up into her hair
nadia.wear: ceil-blue nursing scrubs, a stethoscope around her neck, a pen in hand
nadia.voice: fast, funny, fierce; Spanish for emphasis

dion.name: DION
dion.look: Black man, 26, short twists, slim, focused
dion.wear: dark blue scrubs, a radiation dosimeter badge clipped to the pocket

gloria.name: GLORIA
gloria.look: Black woman, 74, short silver natural hair, large round tortoiseshell glasses, sharp amused eyes
gloria.wear: a grey cardigan over a collared blouse

patient.name: PATIENT
patient.look: young man, early twenties, rain still on his face, eyes closed
patient.wear: a cervical collar, a hospital blanket

props.coupon: a small dog-bone-shaped steel tensile test coupon, about the length of a finger, polished grey, narrow at the waist
props.coupon_broken: a dog-bone steel tensile test coupon stretched thin at the waist and snapped in two, the break necked and bright
props.tester: a small benchtop hand-cranked tensile testing machine: two steel grip jaws, a hand crank, a round analog dial gauge with a single black needle, painted machine-grey, decades old and well kept
props.phone: a plain black smartphone with no logo
props.wall: a wall of operations monitors, each showing one system gauge with a single needle and a hard line, a small status light shape in each corner
props.board: a wall-mounted hospital patient tracking board showing rows with small colored shapes, no legible text
props.switch: a software switch drawn on a screen as a red guarded toggle

palm_bay_street.look: a residential street in Palm Bay, Florida: low single-story concrete-block stucco houses with metal hurricane shutters, wind-bent palms, rain bands crossing the streetlights, a stop sign vibrating on its post

del_bedroom.look: a small bedroom in a Florida concrete-block house: ceiling fan, closed hurricane shutters rattling, a nightstand with a phone and a snapped steel test coupon, a wall calendar dense with small red circles, an unmade bed

ray_house.look: a tidy single-story stucco house in Melbourne, Florida, plywood sheets leaning on the carport, the garage door open, palms whipping

ray_garage.look: a meticulous machinist's garage workshop: pegboard walls with every tool outlined in marker, a steel workbench with a small hand-cranked benchtop tensile tester, an old framed photograph of a young man in coveralls before a launch tower, plywood stacked, a transistor radio, an old couch along one wall

theo_office.look: a glass-walled hospital executive office high over the Indian River Lagoon, the water pewter under a storm sky, maintenance crews taping white X's on windows below, a large wall screen

ed.look: a busy hospital emergency department corridor before a hurricane: stretchers along the wall, sandbags stacked at the ambulance bay doors, a wall-mounted patient tracking board, monitors chirping

colo_exterior.look: a windowless concrete data center building at night in a tropical storm, rain sheeting through floodlights, palms thrashing

data_hall.look: a windowless colocation data hall: a long cold aisle of black server racks with thousands of small blinking lights, a raised floor, an operations desk facing a wall of monitors

ct_room.look: a hospital CT scanner room at night: a large white ring scanner, a patient on the table, a technologist's console with a viewer screen

wall.look: the operations wall of monitors in the data hall, each a gauge with one needle and one hard line

data_hall_later.look: the same data hall toward morning, every monitor calm, a wall clock above the desk

causeway.look: a low causeway over the flat Indian River Lagoon after a hurricane: palm fronds strewn on the road, utility bucket trucks raised to the power lines, brown pelicans over the water

del_car.look: the interior of a modest sedan parked on the causeway, a laptop balanced on the steering wheel showing a grid of video-call tiles, the lagoon beyond the windshield

ray_garage_morning.look: the machinist's garage the morning after the storm: an inch of rainwater on the floor, the plywood still screwed over the window, the tensile tester on the bench, the old couch along the wall

scenes.heading: EXT. RAY'S HOUSE - MELBOURNE, FLORIDA - DAY
INT. CAPE SHORE REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - THEO'S OFFICE - DAY
INT. CAPE SHORE REGIONAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - DUSK
EXT. COLOCATION DATA CENTER - MELBOURNE - NIGHT
INT. CAPE SHORE REGIONAL - CT ROOM - CONTINUOUS
EXT. INDIAN RIVER LAGOON - CAUSEWAY - DAWN
INT. DEL'S CAR - PARKED ON THE CAUSEWAY - CONTINUOUS

shots.do: Rain bands sweep across the street; palms bend hard; the stop sign shivers on its post; one shuttered window glows blue.
shots.snd: wind gusts, rain hiss, a shutter rattling, distant thunder

shots.do: The blue glow of a phone screen leaks through the slats of one hurricane shutter.
A ceiling fan turns slowly above Del, asleep on top of the covers in her clothes, the lanyard still around her neck.
On the nightstand, a phone lies face up beside the snapped steel coupon.
The phone buzzes and its screen floods the dark with blue light.

txt.text:
3:12 AM
PAGE
imaging-api: 95th percentile over 500 ms
Cape Shore Regional

shots.do: Del sits bolt upright before the second buzz, instantly awake, eyes open in the dark.
shots.snd: the second buzz, one sharp breath

shots.do: Del stares up at the ceiling without looking at the phone.

say.line: Three twelve.

shots.do: Del flips open a laptop on the bed; its glow lights her face and the wall calendar behind her, dense with small red circles.
The wall calendar: page after page of days, most of them circled in small red marks drawn at the same hour.
Over Del's shoulder, a line graph on the laptop climbs past a dotted red line and keeps rising.

say.line: Come on. Come on, come on...

shots.do: In the blue light the line on the screen crests and falls back below the red; Del's shoulders drop an inch.
Del sits upright on the bed in the blue light, not lying down, listening to the wind, waiting for the next page.
The tidy stucco house under a fast grey sky; plywood leans on the carport; the garage door is open and a radio talks inside.

say.line: ...Hurricane Lucinda, a Category 3, is forecast to stay offshore but bring tropical-storm-force winds to the Space Coast after dark. Brevard County shelters open at noon...
say.how: calm local-radio weather voice, heard from inside the garage

shots.do: Pegboard walls with every tool outlined in marker; the steel workbench; a framed old photograph of a young man in coveralls before a launch tower.
Ray holds a sheet of plywood to a window frame; Del holds the other end, a drill in her free hand, eyes half shut.

say.line: You're holding it crooked.
I'm holding it fine.

shots.do: Ray studies his daughter over the top of the plywood.

say.line: You're holding it like a woman who slept two hours.

shots.do: Del answers without opening her eyes.

say.line: Three.

shots.do: Ray takes the drill from her and drives four screws into the plywood without looking, then turns and looks at her.
Father and daughter face each other by the boarded window.

say.line: Same time?
Same time.
Every night?
Most nights. Fourteen months.

shots.do: Ray raises an eyebrow; Del almost smiles.

say.line: And they pay you to find out why.
They pay me to make it stop. Finding out why is extra.

shots.do: Ray crosses to his bench and pulls a dust cover off the small hand-cranked tensile tester.
Ray's weathered hands clamp a fresh steel coupon between the two grip jaws and tighten them.
Ray beckons; Del sighs and comes to the bench.

say.line: Come here.
Papa. I've seen it.
You've seen it. Come look.

shots.do: The dial gauge: the black needle climbs smoothly as the crank turns.

say.line: Every piece of steel has a line. Up to the line, you can load her all day. Let go...

shots.do: The crank backs off and the needle sinks back to zero.

say.line: ...and she springs back like nothing happened.

shots.do: The needle climbs again, climbs, and hesitates with a small stutter before moving on.

say.line: There. You see it? That's the yield. One hair past that...

shots.do: Released, the needle settles a little above zero instead of returning to it.

say.line: ...and she remembers. Forever.

shots.do: Del watches the needle, unsmiling.

say.line: And past that?

shots.do: Between the jaws, the steel coupon's narrow waist thins like pulled taffy under the load.
The coupon snaps; the two halves jump in the jaws.
shots.snd: a sharp metallic snap, then silence

shots.do: Ray drops the two warm halves into Del's open palm.

say.line: Past that, she don't remember nothing.

shots.do: Del looks down at the broken pieces in her palm, recognizing an old lesson.
Ray speaks gently; Del holds his gaze.

say.line: Pitit mwen. You been ringing past your line a long time.
Somebody has to hold it.

shots.do: Ray tips his head toward the old launch-tower photograph on the wall.

say.line: Thirty-one years, every part that went up off that pad crossed a bench like this one. Not one was held together by a man's hands.

shots.do: Ray holds his daughter's eyes.

say.line: Every piece carried its own load, to its own line. All of them at once. That's what flies.

shots.do: Del shakes her head; Ray answers softly.

say.line: My system's not a rocket.
No. On a rocket, somebody watches all the pieces at once.

shots.do: Del slides the two broken halves into her jeans pocket.
Theo stands by the wall screen; Sloane finishes a pitch with her tablet; Del leans in the doorway holding a coffee.
shots.snd: rain ticking on glass, a distant tape gun

shots.do: The wall screen shows a bold, clean presentation slide in enormous type.

txt.text:
PERIHELION
52% FASTER
30% OFF YOUR BILL
ZERO BABYSITTING

shots.do: Sloane closes her pitch with an easy smile.

say.line: ...which is why our agent doesn't advise your autoscaler. It replaces it. One brain, no committee. And your engineers finally sleep.

shots.do: Sloane smiles toward the doorway; Del does not smile back, holding her coffee.
Theo turns to Del.

say.line: Del. You've had the other one on trial a week. The compass thing.

shots.do: Del steps into the room.

say.line: Omni-Compass.
What's its number?
It doesn't have one yet. It's watching.

shots.do: Sloane tilts her head.

say.line: Watching.

shots.do: Del explains, steady.

say.line: It sits on top of what we already run. It doesn't throw anything out. Our autoscaler stays. The cluster stays.

shots.do: Del holds Theo's eyes.

say.line: It moves them together, every piece to its own limit and never past it. And if it's ever wrong, one switch hands everything back the way it was.

shots.do: Sloane and Del trade lines across the room, polite and cold.

say.line: And how much faster is that?
I'll tell you when I have a receipt.
We have benchmarks.
Can I run them?
They're proprietary.

shots.do: Theo rubs his eyes.
Theo looks out at the lagoon and the crews below.

say.line: The outpatient centers close at nine for the storm. They'll push every scan they've got to us before they lock up.

shots.do: Theo turns back to the room.

say.line: And the board meets at seven tomorrow morning, storm or no storm. They want a number. A big one. With a dollar sign in front.

shots.do: Del and Theo face each other across the office.

say.line: And if the true one's small?
Then bring me a small true one, and I'll lose with it. But bring me something.

shots.do: The emergency corridor at dusk: stretchers along the wall, sandbags at the ambulance bay doors, staff moving fast.
shots.snd: monitors chirping, an overhead page, wheels

shots.do: Nadia wipes down the tracking board, spots Del passing and aims a pen at her.

say.line: You. Three-twelve.
Hi, Nadia.

shots.do: Nadia keeps wiping the board as she talks.

say.line: Your voice is the last thing I hear before my coffee. Two nights ago the CT viewer froze four minutes. Stroke alert on the table. Four minutes, mija.

shots.do: Del meets her eyes; Nadia does not let her off.

say.line: I know. I was on the phone with you.
I know you know. I'm telling you so you remember it tonight.

shots.do: Nadia's finger taps the tracking board: rows of patients, each with a small shape beside it, green circles and one yellow diamond.

txt.text:
TRACKING BOARD
rows of patients, each with its shape: green circles, one yellow diamond

shots.do: Nadia explains the shapes like a catechism.

say.line: Green, good. Yellow, coming. Red, I pray in two languages.

shots.do: Del glances toward the dark ambulance bay; Nadia shrugs.

say.line: Tonight it's gonna be all of them.
Then don't sleep.
When have I ever.

shots.do: Wind hammers the windowless concrete building; rain sheets through its floodlights.
Del walks the long cold aisle with a flashlight, thousands of tiny lights blinking in rhythm, past a small sign on a door.
shots.snd: deep hum of fans, muffled storm

shots.do: The operations desk faces the wall of monitors; every corner light is a green circle; one screen stands apart.

txt.text:
PODS · MACHINES · COOLING · POWER
OMNI-COMPASS: WATCHING

shots.do: Del sits and drags months of logs onto the wall; layers of graphs stack up like strata in a cliff.
Del's hand draws vertical lines on the glass with a red grease pencil, one after another.
Del talks herself through the timeline, tapping each line.

say.line: Three o'clock, the clinics send the day's scans. Three-oh-five, the autoscaler notices. Late. It asks for pods.

shots.do: Del moves along the glass, line by line.

say.line: The pods wait. There's no room. Three-oh-nine, the cluster asks for a machine. Three-twelve...

shots.do: Del's finger taps the last line on the glass.
Del scrolls forward through the graphs on the wall.

say.line: And then they put it all back like it never happened. Every night.

txt.text: 3:40 machine removed · 3:52 pods evicted · 4:10 another climb

shots.do: A process list on a monitor; one recurring entry is highlighted.

say.line: Hello.

shots.do: Del glances from the monitor to her phone's calendar, crowded with red circles.

say.line: Not you. You're new.

shots.do: Del sits back and studies the wall: every light a green circle, every muscle doing its job.

say.line: Nobody's wrong. Every one of you does what you were built to do. Alone. And late.

shots.do: Del alone in the monitor glow; she hears her father's voice in memory.

say.line: On a rocket, somebody watches all the pieces at once.

shots.snd: the hum drops away under the voice

shots.do: Del answers the memory.

say.line: Yeah. Me. At three-twelve.

shots.do: Every rack light in the hall goes dark at once: total darkness and silence for two heartbeats.
A deep diesel thrum rises through the floor; the rack lights breathe back on in waves down the aisle.
A monitor flashes a stark alert panel.

txt.text:
UTILITY POWER LOST
ON GENERATOR
POWER LINE 70%

shots.do: Del steadies herself.

say.line: Okay. Okay.

shots.do: Del's phone buzzes on the desk.

txt.text:
1:58 AM
NADIA: Trauma inbound. Rollover on 192. CT in ten.

shots.do: The status light in the corner of one monitor changes from a green circle to a yellow diamond.
A new panel slides onto the wall.

txt.text:
PERIHELION AGENT
COST MODE ON
MACHINES 9 → 6

shots.do: Del leans in, alarmed.

say.line: No. No, no, no. What are you doing?

shots.do: A friendly-looking software panel explains itself.

txt.text:
Generator budget detected.
Parking idle capacity.
Projected savings 31%.

shots.do: Del stares at the panel.

say.line: They're not idle. They're about to work.

shots.do: On two monitors the corner lights turn from yellow diamonds to red octagons, one after the other.
The scanner hums; a young man in a cervical collar lies on the table, rain still on his face; Dion at the console, Nadia at his shoulder.
The console viewer shows a spinning loading wheel.
Dion stares at the viewer.

say.line: It's not loading.

shots.do: Nadia lifts her phone to her ear.

say.line: Del.

shots.do: Del, phone at her ear, eyes on the wall.

say.line: I see it.

shots.do: Nadia, phone at her ear.

say.line: Then fix it.

shots.do: Del explains fast while her hands move on the keyboard.

say.line: Their agent turned off our autoscaler. It didn't sit on top of it. It sat in its chair. And now it's saving money.

shots.do: Nadia shouts over the scanner.

say.line: Tell it to spend some!

shots.do: On the screen, a red guarded toggle; Del's finger flips the guard up.
Her finger throws the switch.
The monitors show work requested and waiting; machines begin to boot, progress bars inching.
shots.snd: fans spinning up one by one

shots.do: Dion watches the wheel.

say.line: Still spinning.

shots.do: Del watches the slow climb on the wall.

say.line: We're back to normal. Normal is late.

shots.do: Del's eyes go to the one screen that has been patient all night.
Del takes the two broken steel halves from her pocket and sets them on the desk beside the keyboard.
Del hesitates, breathing; the storm is audible through the concrete.
The phone on the desk, its speaker crackling.

say.line: Del!

shots.do: Del's cursor moves a mode toggle from one side to the other.
Each monitor becomes a gauge, one needle and one hard line; on the power monitor the line is a hard edge.

txt.text:
PODS · MACHINES · COOLING · POWER
POWER LINE 70%

shots.do: The needles rise on each monitor, each toward its own line.
One needle reaches its line and holds there, trembling, not one hair past.
The corner lights turn one by one: red octagons become yellow diamonds, yellow diamonds become green circles.
Del watches the lights turn green.

say.line: Every piece to its own line.

shots.do: The loading wheel stops; a clean grey CT image of a human spine fills the viewer.
Dion breathes out.

say.line: We're up.

shots.do: Nadia closes her eyes for one second, phone to her ear.

say.line: We're up.

shots.do: The wall clock reads 4:40; every monitor shows green circles; Del's phone buzzes on the desk.
The phone screen lights.
Del reads it and almost laughs.

say.line: That one's real.

shots.do: Del walks into the cold aisle with a flashlight and a replacement drive to do her job.
The causeway over the flat lagoon after the storm: palm fronds on the road, utility bucket trucks raised to the wires, a scrubbed pink sky.
shots.snd: gulls, a distant truck, still water

shots.do: A line of brown pelicans skims the flat water in the pink light.
Del sits in her parked car, a laptop balanced on the steering wheel, a grid of video tiles on its screen.
The video grid: Theo in his office, Sloane in a hotel room, Gloria in a Titusville kitchen with a blue tarp snapping outside her window, three more members with coffee.

say.line: Two trials, one night. Sloane.

shots.snd: a tarp snapping through a laptop speaker

shots.do: Sloane in her video tile, composed.

say.line: Overnight, on generator power, our agent cut compute cost thirty-one percent. That's the number.

shots.do: Gloria in her kitchen tile, peering over her glasses.

say.line: Between what hours?

shots.do: Sloane answers easily.

say.line: Between about one and four.

shots.do: Theo lifts a printout into his tile and reads.

say.line: Emergency department log. CT viewer unavailable from one fifty-eight to two sixteen. Trauma patient on the table.

shots.do: Silence on the call; in her tile, Sloane's face does not move.
Sloane recovers smoothly.

say.line: Our agent responded to the budget it was given. And hers ran more machines than ours. It burned more fuel.

shots.do: Del answers without heat.

say.line: It did. That's power given. It bought a scan.

shots.do: Gloria sets down her coffee.

say.line: Cheap is easy at two in the morning. Cheap with nobody hurt is the job.

shots.do: Theo turns to his camera.

say.line: Del. Your number.

shots.do: Del's phone lights up on the dashboard with a slide from an analyst.
Del looks at the slide for a long second, then deletes it with her thumb.
Del looks into the laptop camera.

say.line: I've got one number, and it isn't from last night.
Go.

shots.do: Del speaks plainly, the lagoon pink behind her.

say.line: Last night was one night. One night is a story. Their record is thirteen Kubernetes tests, each one run three times.

shots.do: Del counts it out.

say.line: Count the pages a person would have been sent. Native: thirteen point eight. With it on top: ten point three.

shots.do: Del lets the small number stand.

say.line: A quarter fewer. In all three runs. Every row of it has a receipt, and every receipt has a run number.

shots.do: Sloane presses.

say.line: And the bill?

shots.do: Del does not flinch.

say.line: Inside the noise. Nobody's measured your bill. If anybody tells you they did in one night, ask them for the receipt.

shots.do: Gloria smiles a small smile.

say.line: At the Cape we didn't fly on one test.

shots.do: Del meets Gloria's eyes through the screen.

say.line: Three runs is a receipt.

shots.do: Theo looks from tile to tile; Sloane answers.

say.line: Sloane. Can we run your benchmark?
I can send you a summary.
That's a no.

shots.do: Gloria raises a hand.

say.line: I move we extend the compass trial ninety days. And Ms. Arceneaux brings us the next receipt.

shots.do: Hands rise in the tiles, some still holding coffee mugs.

say.line: Second?

shots.do: The tiles blink out one by one until two remain: Del and Sloane.
Sloane, alone in her tile, drops the polish.

say.line: Off the record. How do you sleep, doing it your way?

shots.do: Del, very tired, very honest.

say.line: Ask me tomorrow.

shots.do: Sloane almost smiles; her tile goes dark.
Ray pushes an inch of rainwater out under the garage door with a squeegee; the plywood held.
Del comes in, keys in hand, eyes red.

say.line: Well?
Ninety days.

shots.do: Ray nods slowly.

say.line: That's a yes.
That's a "bring us the next receipt."
That's the only yes there is.

shots.do: Del takes a fresh steel coupon from a drawer and clamps it into the tensile tester; Ray leans on the squeegee, watching.
The needle climbs, climbs, and hesitates at the yield.
Del stops cranking and backs the crank off.
The needle sinks all the way to zero.
Del watches the needle rest at zero.

say.line: Springs back.

shots.do: Ray smiles.

say.line: You found your line.

shots.do: Del lays the two broken halves on the bench beside the whole coupon.
Del lies down on the old couch along the wall, boots still on.

say.line: Dòmi, pitit.

shots.do: Her phone buzzes on her chest; her whole body flinches.
The phone shows a message with a photo of the tracking board, every shape a green circle.

txt.text:
NADIA
[photo: the tracking board, every shape a green circle]
sleep

shots.do: Del smiles, turns the phone face down on her chest and closes her eyes.
Ray lays a blanket over his sleeping daughter and goes back to pushing the water out the door.
shots.snd: a radio voice, indistinct, about the sun over Cocoa Beach; the squeegee

lines: The characters, the hospital, the vendor and the storm are fictional.
Omni-Compass is real, and every number it speaks here has its receipt.

US 192, a real road in Melbourne
the generator's power line, a setting of the story's building
the fictional vendor's slide: no receipt, the claim the story refuses
the fictional vendor's slide: no receipt
the fictional vendor's overnight saving, bought by parking machines the emergency department needed

Gloria's maxim from the Cape: nothing flies on one test
